in_hebrew.name: טִרְצָאְיָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: טִרְצָאְיָה - פרי ושלום, שם שמקורו בעברית עתיקה ומיוחס למשמעות של 'פרי' ו'שלום', וניתן לפרש כ'פרי שלום' או 'פרי תפארת'. ישנן מספר רב של אפשרויות לניתוח המשמעות של השם, אך כולן חוברות יחדיו למשמעות כללית של פרי-שלום. השם Tirzaya נזכר פעם אחת בספר תהלים, (Psalm 72:17).

in_greek.name: Τιρζαΐα
in_greek.long_meaning: Τιρζαΐα, σπάνια ονομασία με ελληνοεβραϊκή προέλευση, με τυπολογικές ομοιότητες με την εβραϊκή ονομασία 'טִרְצָאְיָה', το οποίο σημαίνει 'πέτρα ελπίδος'.

in_latin.name: Tirzaya
in_latin.long_meaning: Tirzaya, nomen eximium, significat fructum pacis, sicut in nomine Hebraeo-Tyrzaiah. Hoc nomen originalem habet a vocabulis Hebraeis 'Tirz' (fruitus) et 'Aiya' (pax), significans 'fruitum pacis'.

in_english.name: Tirzaya
in_english.meaning: Fruit of Peace, symbolizing abundance and harmony
in_english.long_meaning: Tirzaya, a unique name with Hebrew and Greek roots, is a symbol of the 'Fruit of Peace', representing abundance and harmony. The name is derived from the Hebrew words 'Tirz' (fruit) and 'Aiya' (peace), signifying 'fruit of peace'. In the Bible, the concept of the 'Fruit of Peace' is mentioned in Psalm 72:17, highlighting the significance of peace and harmony in the Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tirzah holds significant cultural relevance in the Hebrew Bible. It is named after the ancient city of Tirzah, one of the capitals of the ancient Israelite kingdom. The city is mentioned several times in the scriptures, indicating its historical importance in Israelite history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tirzah carries a deep spiritual significance, meaning 'God will dew'. This name is a reminder that just as God brings life-giving dew to the thirsty ground, He also brings His divine presence and blessings to His people. It is a powerful evocation of God's love, care, and provision. For those who bear the name Tirzah, it serves as a constant reminder of God's sustaining grace in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tirzah, meaning "delight," is a Hebrew name given to a daughter in the Bible, representing the joy and pleasure derived from her existence. This name also symbolizes the divine grace and beauty bestowed upon her, embodying the essence of God's love and creation.

biblical_reference.note: Tirzaya is mentioned in the Bible as a symbol of the 'Fruit of Peace'.

historical_references.reference: According to the Old Testament book of Judges, Tirzah was the name of a city located in the region of Ephraim. It was one of the capital cities of the northern kingdom of Israel during the time of Jeroboam I (around 931-910 BC). The city was known for its beautiful trees and its importance as a religious center.
historical_references.context: Old Testament, city of the northern kingdom of Israel, capital city, religious center

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament book of Luke (10:38), Tirzah is mentioned as the hometown of Martha, one of the sisters of Lazarus. Martha, along with her sister Mary, welcomed Jesus into their home and provided hospitality to him during his ministry. The town of Tirzah is not further identified in the text.
historical_references.context: New Testament, hometown of Martha, sister of Lazarus, hospitality to Jesus

trends: Alternative Names for Traditional Biblical Characters
modern_usage.modern_context: In modern contexts, the Christian name 'Tirzah' or 'Tirzaya' is often found in discussions related to Neopaganism, Goddess Spirituality, and alternative interpretations of biblical characters. Tirzah is identified as one of the daughters of Jephthah and is sometimes associated with the Goddesses Ishtar and Astarte. On Tumblr, there are numerous blogs and posts dedicated to exploring the symbolism and meanings behind Tirzah's name and her potential connection to these goddesses. Reddit communities, such as r/pagan, provide a space for practitioners to share their experiences and perspectives on Tirzah as a divine figure. Wikipedia entries on Tirzah and related topics offer a more academic approach to understanding her modern significance and various interpretations.
